brief: Goldman's EMEA delta-one desk (Privorotsky) argues AI demand is not the problem; the debate is how much to discount future AI cash flows given the uncertainty around supply, competition and financing. Demand proof points are strong (Celestica, Cadence, Korean memory names, AWS capacity sold out, little chance of memory oversupply through 2029), but Goldman's Hatzius sees the AI capex impulse to GDP peaking near 1.5% in Q4 2026 and falling to roughly 0.6% by end 2027, compounded by a roughly 100bp yield rise adding a cumulative 0.6% of GDP drag. That is why this week's hyperscaler test is binary: capex flat or up is fine, down would be disastrous for picks and shovels. Meta answered by raising up to $97.5 billion in equity rather than debt, Privorotsky's 'middle ground' scenario (bad for equity, potentially good for credit), while its free cash flow turned negative and its CDS widened. Off-balance-sheet hyperscaler obligations now total $2.8 trillion, up eightfold since 2023, and credit stress concentrates in neoclouds. Credit still flags yellow to red versus equities even as a tentative, hedged relief rally builds into Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon earnings and the Fed.
